title: Faultstorm: Synthetic customer-journey chaos to validate SLOs, circuit-breakers, and load-shedding
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Objective: Run an automated, repeatable 'faultstorm' suite that injecs combinations of region loss, GPU pool saturation, and dependency blackholes across synthetic customer journeys to validate SLO boundaries, circuit-breaker behavior, and load-shedding policies.

Background: Recent incidents showed complex cross-region pressure can trigger noisy fallbacks and client-visible latency spikes. We need an end-to-end harness that exercises realistic traffic shapes (inference + embedding + batch requests) across multi-region routing, exercises our admission control and circuit breakers, and produces actionable telemetry for tuning.

Scope: engineering-owned chaos harness and test plan, runbook updates, dashboarding, and recommended config changes. This ticket covers harness development, one experimental run in staging with full telemetry capture, and a follow-up tuning pass. Does NOT include automated production rollout; that will be a separate delivery if experiments pass.

Key artifacts:
- Experiment spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/Faultstorm+Experiment+Spec
- Synthetic journey scenarios (sheet): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/faultstorm-scenarios
- Staging experiment automation (GH): https://github.com/redwood-inference/faultstorm/tree/eng-57134

Constraints and risks:
- Must avoid running destructive experiments against production data; staging will mirror traffic shape but use synthetic inputs.
- GPU pool exhaustion must be rate-limited to avoid impacting other staging tenants.
- Circuit-breaker parameter changes are experimental and must be rolled back by the runbook if regressions occur.
acceptance_criteria: A harness exists that can inject: (a) region routing blackhole, (b) GPU pool CPU/GPU saturation, (c) dependency latency/blackhole or combinations thereof
At least 6 synthetic customer-journey scenarios executed end-to-end in staging with telemetry captured (traces, token-level latency, admission control events, circuit-breaker tripped counts)
Threshold-based assertions for SLOs and degradation behavior implemented and reported (see metrics_to_capture)
A documented tuning recommendation set (circuit-breaker thresholds, admission-control weights, load-shed policies) and a roll-forward / rollback runbook attached
Run results uploaded to Confluence with a postmortem-style summary and next steps
plan: Week 1: Implement harness primitives (region route toggle, simulated GPU pool pressure using cgroups/gpu-sim, dependency blackhole via proxy) and basic orchestration
Week 2: Wire harness to synthetic journey runner, add telemetry hooks (open-telemetry traces, token-latency histograms, admission control counters) and dashboards
Week 3: Execute staged faultstorm runs with incremental blast radius and capture metrics; iterate on canary gating rules
Week 4: Analyze results, propose tuning changes, document runbook and handoff to SRE for potential controlled experiments in pre-prod/prod
test_scenarios: Scenario A: Regional egress blackhole for primary region during steady small-traffic load (validate routing fallback to secondary, verify no retry storm)
Scenario B: GPU pool exhaustion in primary pool during bursty prompt traffic (validate admission control, queue latency, token drop behavior, cost-surrogates)
Scenario C: Dependency blackhole (downstream model store or KMS) under mixed-mode traffic (embedding + generation) to validate graceful degradation and error mapping to clients
Scenario D: Compound failure: primary region blackhole + small GPU pool saturation + high downstream latency (exercise circuit-breakers and coordinated load-shedding across tiers)
Scenario E: Latency spike in control plane (delayed model routing metadata) to evaluate model-variant fallback correctness and rate limiter interactions
Scenario F: Synthetic customer journey with chained tool calls to validate end-to-end observable propagation and SLO attribution
metrics_to_capture: request success rate and error class breakdown (client-error, upstream-error, model-timeout)
circuit-breaker state transitions and counts (open -> half-open -> closed)
cost estimators: token-CPU/GPU utilization and tokens-per-second per-GPU
trace spans showing fallback path (region fallback, model-variant fallback)
downstream dependency call latency and error rates (model-store, KMS, config service)
comments: 2026-02-11 Alyssa Chen: Kickoff with Marco and Priya. Agreed to scope GPU saturation using a non-destructive GPU cgroup simulator; will not evict real jobs. Priya will draft the scenario matrix.

2026-02-17 Marco Rivera: Implemented region-toggle primitive and a proxy shard to simulate dependency blackhole. Deployed to staging cluster 'stg-us' behind feature flag 'faultstorm-region-toggle'. PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/faultstorm/pull/42

2026-02-21 Priya Nair: Added synthetic customer journeys (chat, embedding, batch rerank) and baseline captures. Observed admission-control reject spikes at sustained 120 qps/worker under GPU sim. Documented in sheet.

2026-02-24 Ethan Gold (SRE): Executed Scenario B with guarded blast radius: GPU saturation at 70% for 5 minutes. Observed circuit-breaker open events after ~18s in the model-variant path; fallback to cheaper quantized variant introduced 35% higher latency but maintained success-rate for priority customers.

2026-02-27 Marco Rivera: Analysis shows current circuit-breaker cooldowns are too short; they oscillate under compound failures. Proposal: increase cooldown windows and add rate-limited half-open probes. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1187

2026-02-28 Alyssa Chen: Decided to pause any config rollouts to pre-prod until we finish one more run with adjusted cooldowns. Next run scheduled 2026-03-02. Added follow-up task to SRE to instrument retry headers for easier attribution.

2026-03-01 Priya Nair: Post-run notes uploaded to Confluence. Early recommendation: tune admission-control to prefer graceful degrade (shortened responses) over hard rejects for tiered customers; draft runbook update ready for review.
